correctness.rationale: After removal of either good from a different center, one singleton remains with each of the four hypothetical center comparison valuations at most 1. An active center with no liked owned good has own value 0 and a liked good in another center, so cannot be EFX; every EFX-satisfied active center selects a distinct liked owned good, giving upper bound nu by matching. Allocate maximum-matching goods to liked lower agents and fill all other singletons: each matched center has own realized welfare >=1, satisfying all four EFX constraints, and inactive centers never envy; one-good inter-EF1 is automatic. Hall deficiency follows from standard max matching duality. Three lower agents in each of two centers, three goods liked by all and three liked by none, violates EFX despite Hall, proving capacity restriction. Independent brute force checked 1,075 sampled two-center four-good approval profiles across all 24 one-to-one allocations and all four convention formulas; finite tests corroborate universal elementary proof.

value.rationale: The minimal number of EFX-failing centers is a natural exact infeasibility invariant of a motivated delegated-allocation model, and the polynomial-time algorithm and sharp capacity-three counterexample contrast the general hardness regime. The reduction is elementary only after recognizing the special singleton comparison collapse; not merely a restatement of Hall in its original setting.
